questions.question: What must be true for a finite list $\mathcal V$ to be a spanning list for $V$?
options: $\mathcal V$ contains exactly one vector.
$V=\operatorname{span}(\mathcal V)$.
$\operatorname{span}(\mathcal V)=\{\boldsymbol 0\}$ only.

questions.explanation: A finite list $\mathcal V$ is a spanning list for $V$ exactly when $V=\operatorname{span}(\mathcal V)$, i.e. every vector in $V$ is a linear combination of the list.
